question: How many calendar days does a graduate student have to drop a full-semester class without receiving a transcript grade?
gold_answer: The first 14 calendar days of the term.

question: How long is the add/drop period for half- and graduate third-term classes?
gold_answer: The first 7 calendar days of the term.

question: If a student simply stops attending class, does that count as withdrawing from the course?
gold_answer: No. Not attending class does not constitute withdrawal.

question: Can a graduate student withdraw from a course during the final week of the term?
gold_answer: No. Withdrawals are not accepted during the last week of the term.

question: What are the three major academic terms in Northeastern's semester-based calendar?
gold_answer: Fall semester, Spring semester, and Summer semester.

question: How long is a typical full-semester course at Northeastern?
gold_answer: Approximately 15 weeks, including the final examination period.

question: How many semester hours must a graduate student generally complete before participating in co-op?
gold_answer: 16 semester hours.

question: What cumulative GPA is required to be eligible to search for a graduate co-op position?
gold_answer: A cumulative GPA of 3.000.

question: Can a standard graduate co-op be extended to eight months?
gold_answer: Yes. Extensions to eight months are permitted if applicable requirements are met and the co-op coordinator or advisor approves.

question: Can a student take a class while working a full-time co-op?
gold_answer: Possibly. A student on a full-time co-op may be permitted to take one course outside work hours, subject to college policies.

question: Is CPT authorization specific to the employer, location, dates, and whether the work is full-time or part-time?
gold_answer: Yes. CPT is employer, location, full-time/part-time, and date specific.

question: Does an unpaid experiential learning opportunity require CPT authorization for an eligible F-1 student?
gold_answer: Yes. CPT authorization is required even for unpaid experiential learning opportunities.

question: How long does OGS say it may take to review a completed CPT request?
gold_answer: Up to 15 business days after receiving the completed request.

question: What happens to OPT eligibility if an F-1 student exceeds 364 days of full-time CPT at the same degree level?
gold_answer: The student loses eligibility to apply for OPT at that degree level.

question: What is the minimum number of workdays for a semester full-term co-op?
gold_answer: 55 workdays.

question: What is the minimum number of workdays for a summer session A or B co-op term?
gold_answer: 25 workdays.

question: How many hours per week define a full-time co-op job?
gold_answer: 32 to 40 hours per week.

question: How many hours per week are considered part-time CPT?
gold_answer: 20 hours per week or less.

question: How many hours per week are considered full-time CPT?
gold_answer: More than 20 hours per week.

question: Does Northeastern charge tuition when a student is only on co-op and takes no credit-bearing class?
gold_answer: No tuition is charged when a student is on co-op only.

question: If I disappear from class without formally dropping it, am I automatically withdrawn?
gold_answer: No. Simply not attending class does not constitute withdrawal.

question: How much time do I get at the beginning of a normal semester course to leave it without a grade appearing?
gold_answer: The first 14 calendar days of the term for a full-semester class.

question: What GPA do I need before I can start looking for graduate co-op jobs?
gold_answer: A cumulative GPA of 3.000.

question: Can an unpaid internship still require F-1 CPT approval?
gold_answer: Yes. An unpaid experiential learning opportunity can still require CPT authorization.

question: If I change the employer or work location during CPT, can I just continue using the same authorization?
gold_answer: No. Changes to employer, location, dates, or hours must be reported and approved by the academic or co-op advisor and OGS.

question: Can I work on CPT before OGS approves it if my employer already gave me a start date?
gold_answer: No. CPT authorization must be obtained before the intended start date.

question: If I am doing a remote co-op during a required academic term, do I still need an on-ground component?
gold_answer: Yes. Students doing remote full-time experiential learning during a required term must maintain on-ground presence through a designated on-ground course; remote co-op students may be enrolled in a 0-credit in-person EXED course.

question: Can my graduate co-op last half a year?
gold_answer: Yes. Six months is one of the common graduate co-op patterns.

question: What must an international graduate student do before beginning a Northeastern co-op in the United States?
gold_answer: The student must satisfy graduate co-op eligibility requirements and, if in F-1 status, obtain proper CPT authorization from OGS before beginning employment.

question: Can an F-1 graduate student begin a co-op immediately after receiving an employer offer if the university has not yet approved the co-op or CPT?
gold_answer: No. The co-op must be approved through the university process and CPT authorization must be obtained from OGS before the experiential learning begins.

question: What requirements apply if an F-1 student wants to extend a co-op from six months to eight months?
gold_answer: The student must meet university term, academic program and registrar requirements, receive co-op coordinator or advisor approval, and consult OGS regarding eligibility to extend CPT authorization.

question: If an F-1 student works a remote full-time co-op during a required term, what academic or immigration requirements still apply?
gold_answer: The student must remain properly registered for co-op and maintain required on-ground presence, such as through a university-designated on-ground course or the applicable EXED course.

question: What could happen if a graduate student drops below full-time enrollment while also being an international student?
gold_answer: Dropping below full-time enrollment may affect financial aid, health insurance eligibility, and maintenance of nonimmigrant visa status; F-1 students also have full-time enrollment and status-maintenance obligations.

question: All graduate co-ops must last exactly six months, correct?
gold_answer: No. Common graduate co-op patterns include four, six, and eight months.

question: CPT is only necessary when an internship is paid, right?
gold_answer: No. CPT may be required whether the experiential learning opportunity is paid or unpaid.

question: A student can withdraw from a course at any point in the semester as long as they accept a W, correct?
gold_answer: No. Withdrawals are not accepted during the last week of the term.

question: Part-time CPT counts toward the 364-day full-time CPT limit for OPT eligibility, correct?
gold_answer: No. Part-time CPT of 20 hours per week or less does not accrue toward the 364-day calculation.

question: Once CPT has been approved, students can freely change their work location without contacting OGS, correct?
gold_answer: No. Changes to CPT employment details such as employer location must be reported and approved.
